cover.woman_bio: Born Sarah Breedlove in Louisiana four years after the Emancipation Proclamation, she worked in cotton fields and as a laundress. In 1905 she took the name Madam C.J. Walker and built a hair-care company with a factory in Indianapolis; she is widely called America’s first Black woman self-made millionaire.
cover.quote: I got my start by giving myself a start.
cover.quote_source: Madam C.J. Walker, widely quoted (CNBC, 15 Feb 2017; Gale, 2020)

pomodoros.subject: Writing: join sentences, fix run-ons, build a paragraph (essay first)

content.content: Three ways to join two complete sentences: , and (adds), , but (contrast), , so (result). Or use because to give a reason. Never join two sentences with only a comma or with nothing: that is a run-on.
Model. I was tired. I finished my work. → I was tired, but I finished my work. / I finished my work because I wanted to be done.
Your topic. Madam C.J. Walker said, “I got my start by giving myself a start.” You will write about a start you gave yourself.

content.question: Which one is a run-on?
choices: A) Walker built a factory, and it hired thousands of workers.
B) Walker built a factory it hired thousands of workers.
C) Walker built a factory because she wanted steady work.
D) Walker built a factory, but it took years.

content.question: Join with , so: “Walker had to make her own living. She started her own business.”
hints: Name the two sentences. Each needs a subject and a verb.

content.question: Join with because: “Walker sold her products herself. She wanted to build trust.”
hints: Say the main idea first, then the word because, then the reason.

content.question: Fix the run-on in TWO different ways: “Walker moved to Indianapolis she built a factory it employed many people.”
hints: Count the complete thoughts. Put a period or a comma + joiner between them.

pomodoros.subject: Social Studies: a business life in numbers

content.content: Reading. Madam C.J. Walker was born Sarah Breedlove on December 23, 1867, and died on May 25, 1919. In 1905 she took the name Madam C.J. Walker and began selling her own hair-care products. She later built a factory in Indianapolis.

content.question: How old was she when she died? (Had December 23 come yet by May 25?)
Profit equals:
A business takes in QAR 5,000 and spends QAR 3,200. What is the profit?
Profit margin = profit ÷ revenue × 100. What is the margin? (whole = revenue)
hints: Divide profit by revenue, then multiply by 100.

content.question: Which is a FACT?
choices: A) She was the smartest person of her time.
B) Everyone should start a business.
C) Her products were the best.
D) She took the name Madam C.J. Walker in 1905.

content.question: In 2 complete sentences: why might starting a business in 1905 have been hard for a Black woman in the South?

content.content: Passage. An entrepreneur starts a business and takes the risk that it may fail. Madam Walker did not wait for a job to be offered. She made a product, found customers and built a company that grew into a factory. In her own words she gave herself a start.

content.question: What is the main idea?
choices: B) Walker created her own opportunity by starting a business.
C) Jobs are hard to find.

content.question: In the passage, “entrepreneur” means:
choices: A) A person who works for others
C) A person who sells nothing
D) A person who starts a business and takes the risk

content.question: What can you infer?
choices: A) Walker believed in making her own chances.

content.question: Use entrepreneur in a sentence of your own about someone you know.
